chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام was asked
about a man who vowed to walk to the House, then came upon a crossing. He said: "Then let him stand in the crossing until he passes it."

key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْمِعْبَرِ: the crossing itself where passage occurs
key_terms.مَعْبَرٍ: a crossing place such as a river passage
key_terms.نَذَرَ: made a vow binding himself to an act
key_terms.يَجُوزَهُ: to pass beyond it or complete traversing it
key_terms.يَمْشِيَ: to walk on foot as part of the vowed act

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they vowed to walk to the House of Allah and encountered a river crossing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a vow to walk to the Sacred House when a physical crossing interrupts the journey. It indicates that the vowed state of walking is maintained as far as possible, and when walking is not possible at the crossing, the person pauses there until the crossing is completed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4316 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) was asked
about a man who vowed to walk to the House of Allah (swt) but encountered a river crossing along the way. Imam (as) said: "Let him stand in the crossing until he passes it."
